overview.heading: What is a Bachelor of Physiotherapy?
paragraphs: Bachelor of Physiotherapy is a four-year undergraduate health course, often followed by compulsory internship time, that trains students to assess movement problems, reduce pain, and help people recover after injury, surgery, stroke, or illness. It is a practical course with anatomy, physiology, exercise therapy, electrotherapy, and clinical training.

Students spend a lot of time in labs and clinical settings, not just classrooms. The work suits people who want direct patient contact and enjoy understanding how the body moves. Admission is usually after Class 12 Science with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, and some colleges also require English and a minimum score.

After graduation, a physiotherapy licence or registration is usually needed before practising independently as a physiotherapist. A BPT can lead to hospital, private clinic, sports rehabilitation, home care, and teaching or research roles later, often after further study and experience.

snapshot.data_note: In India, pay for physiotherapy graduates changes with experience, city, employer type, and the work setting. Private hospitals, clinics, sports rehab centres, home-care work, and teaching or research can sit in very different pay bands, so one figure cannot describe every starter job.

salary.note: Mainstream published ranges for BPT graduates in India place starting pay around 2 LPA, with many physiotherapist roles averaging around 3.2 to 4.5 LPA and higher pay for experienced, specialist, or academic roles.

caution.heading: Be careful if you expect this course to be mostly fitness or gym work
points: The job is clinical and patient-facing, so comfort with sick, injured, or older patients matters more than sports enthusiasm alone.
Recovery can be slow, so patience and steady follow-up are part of the work; quick visible results are not guaranteed.
A physiotherapist often needs physical stamina for long standing hours, repeated demonstrations, and careful manual work.
Entry into independent practice is not just the degree; a practice licence or registration is part of the path in many roles.

good_fit.heading: You may like this course if you
points: Enjoy biology, anatomy, and understanding how the body works.
Prefer practical learning, lab work, and clinical observation over theory alone.
Are calm, patient, and able to explain exercises clearly to different kinds of people.
Want a healthcare career focused on movement, recovery, and rehabilitation.

curriculum.assessment_methods: Continuous internal assessment, practical laboratory examinations, case presentations, clinical postings, written university examinations, and final internship evaluation.
curriculum.learning_activities: Lectures, anatomy and physiology labs, demonstrations, supervised hospital rotations, patient assessment practice, treatment planning, case discussions, community posting, research/project work, and compulsory internship.

faqs.answer: BPT usually takes 4 to 4.5 years in India, including the compulsory internship year in many programmes.
faqs.question: How long is Bachelor of Physiotherapy?

faqs.answer: Most colleges expect Class 12 Science, usually with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. Some institutions also set a minimum percentage and may use merit or entrance-based admission.
faqs.question: What do students need after Class 12?

faqs.answer: The course is practical and clinical. Students learn anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise therapy, and patient rehabilitation, then apply them in labs and hospital settings.
faqs.question: What do students study in BPT?

faqs.answer: A graduate can work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, sports clinics, outpatient clinics, elder-care services, and community health settings.
faqs.question: Where can a physiotherapy graduate work?

faqs.answer: In India, physiotherapy practice is a regulated health profession. After graduation, graduates usually need the required registration or recognition under the relevant health-professions framework before working independently where the rules apply.
faqs.question: Can a BPT graduate practice right away?

faqs.answer: The degree can lead to further study such as MPT or specialisation in orthopaedics, neurology, cardiopulmonary care, sports physiotherapy, or paediatrics.

parent_corner.intro: Bachelor of Physiotherapy suits students who like science, hands-on learning, and helping people recover movement and independence. It is not a desk-based degree: students spend time in anatomy labs, movement and exercise practice, and supervised clinical work with patients. Families should look at three things early: whether the college has recognised clinical training, whether the admission route matches the student’s Class 12 subjects and marks, and whether the child is comfortable working closely with sick, injured, or older patients. After graduation, practice is tied to professional rules, so internship and registration matter, not just the degree certificate. If your child enjoys biology, patient interaction, and steady practical work, this course can be a strong fit.
